cues.text: A sixty-year-old woman with a previous history of gallstones has colicky abdominal pain and vomiting.
Her abdomen is distended and her bowel sounds are increased.
She is often constipated, but feels that this is different.
This is a story of bowel obstruction, which may be due to gallstone ileus.
A plain abdominal X-ray, an AXR, may show dilated loops of bowel, and perhaps the gallstone itself.
The other patients needed ultrasound, PTC or ERCP instead.
So the correct pairing is this woman with a plain abdominal X-ray.
